title: pricing-decision-matrix-and-exception-workflow-for-corporate-contracts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a clear decision matrix and formal exception workflow for enterprise contract pricing that ties discount approval thresholds to a combined commercial and security-questionnaire (SQ) risk score. Goal is to reduce cycle time for sales, improve auditability of deviations from the pricebook, and ensure larger discounts require commensurate security and compliance signoff when customer data sensitivity is high.
proposal_summary: Introduce a two-dimensional decision matrix (commercial leverage vs. security risk) that computes a suggested discount band and required approvers. Implement an exception request form in Salesforce/Confluence linked to Linear tickets that gathers minimal audit fields (deal size, ARR, recommended discount, SQ score, required controls). Exceptions above the pricebook cap route to Tier 2 pricing committee + Security Reviewer; low-risk, low-discount exceptions can be auto-approved by CRO delegate.
acceptance_criteria: Decision matrix documented and uploaded to Confluence (design + examples)
Exception request template created with required fields and stored in the deals workspace
Approval routing map implemented as a draft (roles + SLAs) and validated with Legal, Security, and Sales Ops
2 example historical deals re-scored against the matrix showing consistent recommendations
Automation spec for future Salesforce/Hub routing created (stubbed integrations)
decision_points: Thresholds for discount bands (e.g., 0-10%, 10-25%, 25-40%, >40%) and how they scale with ARR tiers
How SQ score is calculated and normalized (source: existing security questionnaire scoring + mandatory controls flag)
Who is authorized to approve exceptions at each discount+SQ cell (roles vs named approvers)
Whether to require a separate Security Attestation for discounts >25% when SQ score indicates high data sensitivity
Escalation SLAs (e.g., Tier 1: 48h, Tier 2: 5 business days) and on-call coverage for urgent enterprise deals
open_questions: Can we reuse existing SQ scoring telemetry or do we need a lightweight parallel rubric for pricing?
What is the minimum set of controls that must be present for auto-approve low-risk discounts?
Should we tie discount velocity (frequency of exceptions by account) back into sales comp or quota crediting guidelines?
How will refunds/credits be handled if post-signature security review fails after an exception was granted?
Data retention and audit trail requirements for exception forms (Legal input needed)
comments: 2025-01-10 Aisha Patel: Created ticket after review with Sales Ops. Initial ask: reduce time-to-yes for enterprise while keeping security signoff for sensitive workloads.

2025-01-22 Marcelo Ruiz: Met with Security (Leah) and Legal (Jon). Security is supportive but wants SQ score transparency; Legal requires a mandatory attestation field for data residency and breach notifications.

2025-02-03 Sales Ops (Ravi): Provided dataset of 180 enterprise deals with discount and win-rate; initial matrix backtest shows 12% of deals would have required escalation under the proposed thresholds.
2025-02-14 Design review (Monica): Mocked exception form UI and minimal fields to keep seller time < 4 minutes. Preview attached to Drive folder.
2025-02-21 Marcelo Ruiz: Draft routing map circulated to Pricing Committee. Committee suggested adding a 'Strategic Exec Approval' bucket for co-selling/partner-led deals.

2025-02-28 Aisha Patel: Incorporated committee feedback and submitted matrix to Pricing Committee for final sign-off; requested Legal to confirm audit retention policy by 2025-03-07. Moving ticket to In Review.
